questions.heading: A Rate Case Turns Capital Into Rates Through the Rate Base
questions.stem: A utility places a $2,000k substation in service with a 20-year straight-line book life and a 10% allowed return. The commission uses the end-of-year net plant as the rate base. Leaving out taxes and O&M, what does the substation add to year 1's revenue requirement?

options.text: $200k: the return on the full cost, with no depreciation in it
options.says: Depreciation is part of every year's revenue requirement: it is how the capital is returned, $100k a year here.

options.text: $290k: $100k of depreciation plus a return on $1,900k
options.says: Right: depreciation is $2,000k / 20 = $100k, and the return is 10% of the net plant left at year end, $1,900k.

options.text: $300k: $100k of depreciation plus a return on $2,000k
options.says: The rate base is net of accumulated depreciation, so the return is earned on $1,900k, not the full cost.

options.text: $2,000k: the full cost, recovered in its first year
options.says: Only an operating expense is recovered dollar for dollar in its year; capital is recovered over the asset's life.

questions.heading: A Program Is a Line of Work, and the Portfolio Is Everything Competing for the Same Money
questions.stem: A utility's three programs ask for $30,000k in all against $18,000k of yearly budgets, and no program has an envelope of its own. In the plan an optimizer like GridCap's returns, what decides how much each program receives?

options.text: Each program gets the same fraction of its request, scaled to fit
options.says: GridCap's plan gave transmission 26,720 of 43,990 requested and vegetation 3,120 of 3,900: very different fractions.

options.text: The solver first sets an envelope for each program, then selects
options.says: Envelopes are set before selection by people, never by the optimizer; here there was none.

options.text: Each program gets its must-do projects' cost and nothing beyond it
options.says: GridCap's plan funds 27 projects, far more than its 4 must-dos, in every program.

options.text: Each share is whatever maximizes total value under all the rows
options.says: Right: with no program envelope imposed, each program's share is whatever maximizes NPV under the budgets and floors.

questions.heading: The Capital Plan Is a Selection Under Budgets the Optimizer Did Not Set
questions.stem: A vice president asks the optimization team: "How much should we spend on capital in 2029?" Following the lesson, what should the model's answer be?

options.text: Several plans, one per candidate budget, each with what it buys
options.says: Right: the budget is a business and regulatory decision; the model shows what each budget would buy.

options.text: One budget, found by a budget variable with a cost in the objective
options.says: The design note advises against letting the optimizer set the budget: no one would have authorized it.

options.text: The 2029 spend of the must-do projects, since nothing else is required
options.says: Budgets are set by management and finance; must-dos are one input to the plan, not the budget.

options.text: Every 2029 request in full, since every request is a candidate
options.says: GridCap's requests are 1.65 times its budgets; funding every request is not a plan the budgets allow.
